title: The Long Ledger
premise: In 1911, Freya Sterling, an apprentice clockmaker of quiet habits, is summoned to the cliffside observatory to repair its failing master clock just as the season's first storm closes the only bridge to town. Trapped among astronomers and their staff, she discovers a hidden ledger of debts and favors kept by the late head astronomer — including an unfulfilled promise made in peacetime to a man now declared an enemy national and scheduled for deportation on the morning tide. As suspicion tightens around the observatory, Freya must choose between duty to her guild and keeping that promise, racing the clockwork she herself restored. She honors the promise at great personal cost, the ship sails without him, and Freya inherits both the ledger and a found family bound by what they chose over what was required.
about_author: Elodie Zhou is a former museum conservator who spent years restoring maritime instruments before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about people whose careful hands hide restless hearts.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Freya Sterling, POV. A guild letter sends her up the coast road to repair the observatory's failing master clock; her master is ill, so she goes alone, nervous about being a woman apprentice in a man's errand. Beat: cautious hope, first sight of the tower against a bruising sky.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes Slow
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. She opens the great clock and finds it deliberately sabotaged — a filed tooth, a shifted weight. The astronomers are evasive; the young assistant, Tomas, watches her too closely. Beat: unease beneath professional pride.

chapters.title: The Bridge Goes Down
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The storm takes out the bridge planks; the road home is gone until spring. Supplies are counted, tempers flare, and Freya realizes she is a guest who cannot leave. Beat: claustrophobia settling into reluctant belonging.

chapters.title: The Late Keeper's Room
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Sent to clear the dead head astronomer's study, she finds a locked drawer and, inside it, a ledger of debts and promises — one entry marked unpaid: a life owed to 'A.V.' Beat: curiosity sharpening into moral weight.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Table
chapters.summary: Housekeeper Mrs. Vane, POV. A new arrival — Anton Vogel, a foreign-born instrument maker — joins the winter household under a cloud of official letters. Freya recognizes the initials from the ledger. Beat: dread disguised as courtesy.

chapters.title: What Peacetime Promised
chapters.summary: Anton, POV. He tells Freya, obliquely, how the old astronomer once hid him from conscription and swore the debt would be honored 'by whoever keeps the clock.' Beat: two guarded people circling a shared secret.

chapters.title: Guild Rules
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. A telegram arrives: war tensions have escalated; enemy nationals are to be detained and deported on the first spring packet. Freya weighs her guild oath against the ledger's promise. Beat: duty pressing like a thumb on a mainspring.

chapters.title: Small Repairs
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Winter routines knit the household together — chess, mended roofs, Freya teaching Tomas gear-cutting. Found family forms around the dinner table. Beat: warmth that makes the coming betrayal costlier.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane, POV. One of the staff has been writing to the authorities. Suspicion falls on everyone; Vane quietly burns a letter she shouldn't have read. Beat: loyalty tested in small, deniable acts.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. She finishes repairing the master clock and, in doing so, works out how the sabotage was done — and by whom inside the house. Beat: triumph curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries
chapters.summary: Anton, POV. Anton confesses his full history to Freya: the old astronomer saved him twice, and the second debt was never paid. He asks nothing — which makes it unbearable. Beat: love beginning against both their judgments.

chapters.title: The Constable's Visit
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Officials arrive early to verify the household roster; Freya lies smoothly for the first time in her life and hates how easily it comes. Beat: the point of no return crossed quietly.

chapters.title: What Tomas Saw
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas discovers Freya copying ledger pages and feels betrayed — he reported his own doubts to the constable weeks ago. Beat: the found family cracks along its oldest fault line.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane, POV. Ice breaks on the river; the packet ship is announced for the morning tide ten days hence. Preparations begin, and every kindness becomes a countdown. Beat: time itself becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Saboteur's Reason
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. She confronts the staff member who sabotaged the clock — he stalled repairs hoping to delay the roster verification and save Anton himself. Beat: enemies revealed as allies; guilt redistributed.

chapters.title: A Promise Weighed
chapters.summary: Anton, POV. Anton decides to surrender rather than make the household complicit. Freya argues him out of it with the ledger open between them: a promise unkept is a debt that never closes. Beat: love stated plainly, at last.

chapters.title: Forged Papers
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. With Tomas's grudging help, Freya alters the transit documents using engraver's tools from her kit. Every stroke feels like perjury and prayer at once. Beat: highest tension before the climax.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Tide
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The household holds a silent supper; Vane packs food; Tomas stands watch; the constable's lantern crosses the yard. Beat: held breath, tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. At the dock, the plan nearly fails when the constable boards; Anton walks past him on forged papers while Freya distracts the officer with a fault in the harbor clock. Beat: climax — the promise kept as the gangplank rises.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The officials find discrepancies; Freya accepts blame to shield the others and faces suspension from the guild. Tomas, ashamed, testifies in her defense. Beat: grief and grace arriving together.

chapters.title: The Ledger Closes
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. A letter comes from across the water — Anton safe, the debt acknowledged, a pressed flower enclosed. The guild, moved by the household's testimony, stays her expulsion. Beat: release after long compression.

chapters.title: Whoever Keeps the Clock
chapters.summary: Freya, POV. Spring opens the bridge; Freya chooses to stay as the observatory's keeper of clocks and of the ledger, adding a new first entry: the household's names. Beat: resolution — memory, family, and love outlasting duty's cold arithmetic.
